spec.cell: eras[era][book].churn_alpha_bp_mean (the E99 LEVEL), recomputed with E103's recipe: the era's last decision end priced through the next decision of the same book
spec.split: level_arm = equal-weight mean over THAT arm's own transitions, so each shared transition contributes a_gap/n_gap - a_unscreened/n_unscreened; one-sided dates contribute their own term; residual = delta - sum(pieces) is published, never assumed 0
spec.name_rule: the names published per window are the holdings that appear in one arm and not the other at that decision plus the engine's own entrant/exit lists (truncated to 10/8)
spec.move_rule: a cell is LARGE when |delta| >= 50bp, the threshold the two published moves (745.9 / 1098.3) are read at

cells.skipped: no measurable churn cell for both arms in this era

answers.reading: the two arms hold the same names at every top window that carries a large move, so the delta is a PRICE-READ difference, not a composition difference
answers.reads_as: the 4 largest arm deltas are split into named windows: 2021_2023/mid -1117.2bp -> delta_is_one_window (2021-05-17, top-3 share 58.8%); 2021_2023/me -1098.3bp -> delta_is_one_window (2021-06-30, top-3 share 61.6%); 2017_2020/me -745.9bp -> delta_is_one_window (2020-12-31, top-3 share 100.0%); 2024_now/mid -241.0bp -> delta_is_one_window (2024-01-15, top-3 share 100.0%)

honest: descriptive census only: no gate, no verdict on the strategy, no prereg, no trial count, no ledger booking
an equal-weight mean of name-level reads is not a portfolio return: the split moves a reading, not money
the split is exact for THIS panel at THIS cutoff; a refreshed panel can add or lose a decision date and move the one-sided terms, which is why they are published separately from the shared ones
naming a window names the swap that carried the reading; it does not claim the repair caused the forward returns inside it
